ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a slender geometric figure, with a vertex at the top, beside which a reflex angle of 330° is marked; two long sides extend downward from the top. At the lower-left corner, 20° is marked between the left long side and a slanted line going toward the upper right. In the middle of the figure there are two slanted lines intersecting, and a right-angle mark at the intersection indicates that the included angle between the two slanted lines is 90°. At the lower-right corner, the angle between the right long side and another slanted line is marked with a question mark. Reasoning: The 330° marked at the top is a reflex angle, so the small interior angle between the two long sides is 360° - 330° = 30°. Let the unknown angle at the lower-right corner be x. Looking at the turning-angle relationship along the path from the lower-left slanted line to the lower-right slanted line, passing through the two long sides at the top, the angle between these two intersecting slanted lines is equal to 20° + 30° + x. Since the intersection of these two slanted lines in the figure is marked as a right angle, 20° + 30° + x = 90°. Therefore x = 90° - 50° = 40°.

raw_record.question_text: How big is the angle indicated with a question mark?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as follows: the top vertex has a reflex angle labeled 330°, so the small interior angle between the two long sides is 360°−330°=30°. The lower-left angle between the left long side and the rising diagonal is 20°. The crossing of the two diagonals has a marked right angle, so the angle between those diagonals is 90°. Let the question-mark angle at the lower right be x. Angle-chase along the broken turn from the left diagonal to the right diagonal through the top: the total angle between the two diagonals is 20°+30°+x. Set 20°+30°+x=90°, giving x=40°.
